The page therefore either carries a faded, ghosted duplicate of that text or the two scans overlap. A few further faint lines near the bottom cannot be read. No new mathematics is legible. Below I reconstruct the content that is visible, i.e. the previous page's text.

(1) ROUNDING IN Z[ε], ε^2+ε+1=0. Problem: given rational coordinates a, b, c, find the integer of Z[ε] nearest to α = a+bε+cε².
- The representation is redundant: α is unchanged if t is subtracted from all three coefficients, since 1+ε+ε²=0.
- Let p ≤ q ≤ r be the fractional parts of a, b, c in increasing order. If p=q=r, then α itself is integral.
- Otherwise, choose t in the largest of the three circular gaps (p,q), (q,r), (r,1+p).
- Then [a-t]+[b-t]ε+[c-t]εε is 'the nearest whole number'.
- Reason (mine): with N(x+yε+zε²) = ((x-y)²+(y-z)²+(z-x)²)/2, placing the cut t in the largest gap minimises the spread of the three remainders a-t-[a-t], etc. Those remainders then lie in an interval of length at most 2/3.

(2) CYCLOTOMIC INTEGERS, ε a primitive n-th root of unity, n prime.
- Let f(ε) = a+bε+cε²+... and m = ∏_{j=1}^{n-1} f(ε^j), the norm ('Determinans').
- Let F(ε) = m/f(ε) = ∏_{j≠1} f(ε^j) = A+Bε+Cε²+...
- Finite Fourier inversion gives nA_k = Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} ε^{-kj} F(ε^j). In particular nA = F1+Fε+Fε²+..., nB = F1+ε^{-1}Fε+ε^{-2}Fε²+..., and so on.
- For j ≥ 2, F(ε^j) contains the factor f(ε), so it is divisible by f(ε). Hence nA-F1 ≡ Fε, nB-F1 ≡ ε^{-1}Fε, nC-F1 ≡ ε^{-2}Fε (mod fε).
- Therefore nA-F1-ε^k(nA_k-F1) ≡ 0 (mod fε).
- Differencing consecutive relations gives n(A-B) - εn(B-C) ≡ 0.
- Since n = unit·(1-ε)^{n-1} and fε is prime to 1-ε, n can be cancelled. Hence ε ≡ (A-B)/(B-C) ≡ (B-C)/(C-D) ≡ ... (mod fε).
- Consequence: the root r of x^n≡1 (mod m) that corresponds to the factor fε can be computed from the coefficients of m/fε.
errors: The image of 6v shows essentially no independent legible content. What is faintly visible duplicates the previous page's text, so nothing new can be checked for this folio.

In the underlying argument, the hypothesis 'fε, fεε, ... mutually prime' is not needed for F(ε^j), j≠1, to be divisible by fε. That holds automatically because F(ε^j) contains the factor f(ε). Coprimality matters only for cancelling factors, and for a single correspondence ε ≡ r being well defined modulo m.

The rounding rule is stated without proof. It is correct, but it yields a nearest point only in the sense of minimising the spread of the remainders. That this coincides with minimal norm needs the (true) argument via ((x-y)²+(y-z)²+(z-x)²)/2.

results.what: Nearest-integer (rounding) algorithm in the Eisenstein integers using the redundant coordinates a+bε+cε² and a cut t in the largest gap of the fractional parts
results.modern_name: Closest-vector rounding in the A2 (hexagonal) lattice; Euclidean algorithm in Z[ω]
results.usually_credited_to: Euclideanity of Z[ω]: Gauss/Eisenstein era (Eisenstein 1844); the lattice-rounding method in A_n coordinates: Conway–Sloane (1982)

results.what: Recovering the root r of x^n≡1 mod m attached to the prime factor fε, via ε ≡ (A-B)/(B-C) mod fε, from the coefficients of m/fε
results.modern_name: Identification of the residue of ζ modulo a degree-one prime ideal of Z[ζ]; finite Fourier inversion
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1839) and Kummer (1840s) on cyclotomic integers
